interest: Documents Occupation efforts to end imperial school rituals and features Setsuko Hani's feminist critique of patriarchal family structures.
overview: This file documents Allied Occupation-era reforms of Japanese customs and social structures between October 1947 and July 1948. It includes U.S. State and War Department records on the Japanese Ministry of Education's abolition of school emperor-worship rituals and ceremonial bowing toward the Imperial Palace, alongside Tokyo Despatch No. 428 transmitting Setsuko Hani's monograph on the feudal family system, the Meiji Civil Code, and women's rights.
